evidence: The ALD equipment (TFS: 200, BENEQ Co., Finland) was used to deposited Cu film. Copper (II)-hexafluoroacetylacetonate [Cu(hfac)2] was used as the Cu source, and optical glass (Yinxing Optical Co., Ltd, China) was used as substrates. Cu thin films were deposited onto substrates using [Cu(hfac) 2] and diethylzinc (ZnEt 2) as ALD precursors. High-purity nitrogen served as both the carrier and purging gas. The N 2 flow rate was 300 cm 3 min−1.Z n E t2 and [Cu(hfac)2] were evaporated at 20 °C and 70 °C, respectively. The process cycle consisted of exposure to [Cu(hfac) 2] for 800 ms, purging with N2 for 4 s, exposure to ZnEt2 for 300 ms, and purging with N 2 for 2 s. The Cu thin films were grown at temperatures of 180 °C–200 °C under a pressure of 4 mbar.
